fields.meta_title: Rental History Form: Verify Past Landlords | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a rental history form that emails past landlords six questions, attaches the applicant's signed consent and saves each answer to your table.
fields.h1: Build a Rental History Form That Checks With Past Landlords
fields.hero_description: A rental history form asks the people who rented to your applicant before you did. Emergent builds the request, the signed authorization and a table of every answer.
fields.features_subheading: An application says where someone lived. These six features get the landlord who rented to them to say how it went.
fields.feature_1:
Six questions for the past landlord

Asks for the tenancy dates and monthly rent, then whether rent arrived on time and proper notice was given. It ends on damage and one blunt question: would you rent to them again?
fields.feature_2:
The applicant's signed authorization

Captures the applicant's signature and the date on a statement allowing you to contact each landlord they list. Every request carries the signed copy for the landlord to open.
fields.feature_3:
A private link for each landlord listed

Emails every landlord the applicant names a link to the reference form, with no account to create. Each answer is saved to the applicant's row as soon as the landlord submits.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders for references that stall

Sends a reminder when a past landlord has not replied within the delay you set, then alerts your leasing team in Slack or by email. Each file shows which reference is outstanding.
fields.feature_5:
The application beside the reference

Places the dates and rent the applicant wrote next to what each landlord confirmed, in a table you own. Differences beyond the tolerance you set are flagged for a person.
fields.feature_6:
Every line of the app in your repo

Exports the full source to your GitHub repo. Connect it to your property software or screening service through an API, or change any question by describing the edit in a prompt.

fields.tab_content_1:
Six answers back from every past landlord

Ruth Okafor rents out a one-bedroom above her shop. Applicants list their last two landlords and sign an authorization on the same form. Each landlord gets an emailed link with six questions, ending with whether they would rent to the applicant again. Both replies land in the applicant's row.
fields.tab_content_2:
Move-out dates that disagree go to a leasing agent

Northwind Property Group checks every applicant's most recent landlord before a lease goes out. Its table sets the move-out date the applicant gave beside the date the landlord confirmed. A gap of more than 30 days never turns into a silent no: the file goes to a leasing agent, who asks the applicant what happened.
fields.tab_content_3:
Any landlord who stays quiet gets reminded

Cedar Row Leasing once waited weeks on landlords who never wrote back. Now it gives each one two days before an email reminder goes out. With no reply by day five, the file is flagged for a phone call, and the applicant's status reads as waiting on a reference, not declined.
fields.tab_content_4:
Signed authorization or no reference at all

Requests about former tenants reach Alder Street Management every week. Its reply form answers only when the tenant's signed authorization is attached, and holds anything without it. Dates and rent fill from the company's property software through its API, and a manager confirms the rest.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Rental History Form
fields.howto_description: Settle how far back you check before you write a single question. The requests and the follow-up depend on that answer.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Choose how far back to check
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for every landlord in that window
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick a window, such as the last three years or the last two addresses, and use it for every applicant. A fixed window keeps checks consistent between applicants and tells each one exactly which landlords belong on the list.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Collect each address with move-in and move-out dates, the monthly rent and the reason for leaving. Ask for the landlord or manager by name with a phone and email, and let the applicant flag a landlord they cannot reach and explain why.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add a plain statement that the applicant permits you to contact each past landlord, followed by a signature and the date. Place it ahead of the submit button. Every request you send later carries that signed copy with it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste your window, the six reference questions and the reminder timing into the prompt. Emergent builds the applicant's section, the landlord's reference form and a table that holds both. Reword any question later by asking for it in plain English.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Each landlord the applicant lists gets an email with a private link and the signed authorization attached. No account is needed to reply. Set the reminder delay, and choose who on your team hears about a reference that has gone quiet.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Read what each landlord confirmed against what the applicant wrote. Set a tolerance for dates and rent, and send anything outside it to a person. That person asks the applicant about the difference before any decision is made on the file.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Hold every applicant to the same written rental history standard, for example no unpaid balance owed to a past landlord. Record the decision and its reason on the applicant's row, next to the references it rests on.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is rental application templates whose rental history section is a list of past addresses the applicant types, and the image pack is blank verification PDFs (eForms, Legal Templates, Jotform). None of them closes the loop with the previous landlord. This page is the request a landlord sends that landlord: the applicant's signed authorization, six questions only a past landlord can answer (tenancy dates, rent, late payments, notice given, damage, would rent again), reminders when nobody replies, and the answers set beside what the applicant wrote.
tab_stories: An independent landlord renting a one-bedroom gets an applicant's last two landlords and a signed authorization, and each past landlord answers six questions from an emailed link that lands in the applicant's row.
A property manager's table sets each applicant's stated move-out date beside the one the past landlord confirmed, and any gap over 30 days goes to a leasing agent instead of an automatic no.
A leasing office whose references stall sends a reminder after two days and flags the file for a phone call on day five, so a silent landlord never holds an applicant in limbo.

A management company that answers requests about its former tenants replies only when the tenant's signed authorization is attached, and fills dates and rent from its own property records before a manager confirms.

claims_to_source: Consumer reporting agencies may not report most negative information older than seven years, or bankruptcies older than 10 years; records of criminal convictions have no such limit
Many tenant screening companies on the CFPB list give one free copy of your report every 12 months on request

Landlords buy consumer reports for housing purposes, and when a landlord denies an application or requires a co-signer or larger deposit based even partly on a consumer report, the landlord must give an adverse action notice naming the reporting company, and the applicant can get a free copy within 60 days
Credit reporting companies must investigate a dispute, usually within 30 days, unless they consider it frivolous
Tenant screening reports can be disputed with the screening company, which generally has 30 days to investigate
